metaDescription: Six threshold ramps for interior doors, bathrooms, and hallways, compared on rise, size, rated load, and how each is trimmed, glued, or laid loose.
introParagraphs: Interior doorways are where most threshold ramps end up working. Bathroom sills, closet tracks, sliding-door channels, and the raised edge between a hallway and a bedroom all create a small lip that catches wheels and shuffling feet. This group leans toward those indoor spots, with ramps that range from a trimmable half-inch strip to a full one-inch rubber wedge.

We evaluated six ramps based on product specs and buyer feedback, using each listing's stated rise, size, material, rated load, and installation method. At this budget level you can expect molded rubber, a couple of well-documented capacity ratings, and one cut-to-fit option. Every product here is listed at or under the cap, and the choice mostly depends on how your doorway is built.

Accessibility advice applies. A ramp does not remove every hazard, and its performance depends on correct sizing and placement. Check the rise with a ruler, think about the person and the device, and ask a therapist if the slope or the device is a concern.

products.name: Nuvium 0.6 Inch Rubber Threshold Ramp for Doorways
products.description:
Nuvium builds this wedge from dense, flexible natural rubber and lists it at 0.6 inch high, 3.1 inches long, and 35.5 inches wide. The maker states a 2,000 lb capacity and gives it deep grooves for traction in wet or dry conditions. It covers a standard interior doorway width in one piece.

Because the run is short, the slope works out near 1:5, which is steeper than many people expect from a ramp. The listing admits that a mild rubber odor and a slight curve may be present when it arrives. Both usually settle after the ramp lies flat for a while.

Against the Henka 0.6 inch model, this one gives a higher capacity and full dimensions, but it has no adhesive. Compared with LIEKUMM at 3/8 inch, it suits a taller sill. For a bathroom or bedroom door where the lip is a bit over half an inch, it is the most dependable choice. Place it square across the frame and check that it sits flat before anyone crosses.
products.bestFor: Interior doors with a sill a little over half an inch tall.
pros: Full 0.6 by 3.1 by 35.5 in size listed
Stated 2,000 lb capacity is generous
Deep grooves aid traction in wet or dry
Flexible natural rubber for indoor use
cons: Short run makes for a steep slope
New rubber may carry a mild odor
Curve may need days to flatten out

products.name: Henka 0.6 Inch Rubber Threshold Ramp for Home Entrance
products.description:
Henka's rubber ramp bridges a 0.6 inch rise and comes with a strong self-adhesive base. The maker lists a 1,500 lb capacity and describes the deep grooves as forming drainage channels. It is also described as weather resistant, so it can serve an entry door as well as an interior one.

Adhesive is both its best feature and its main risk. Once you press it into place, it is difficult to reposition, so measure and align first. The listing gives little size information, and you will want the length and width before you buy.

Nuvium's 0.6 inch model offers more capacity and clearer dimensions, but you must hold it in place yourself. Henka solves that by sticking down, which suits a bathroom floor where a wedge might creep on a smooth tile. Clean and dry the surface fully and press along the whole width. For a floor you cannot mark, try a small patch of adhesive somewhere hidden first.
products.bestFor: Smooth tile or vinyl sills where a loose wedge tends to creep.
pros: Backing sticks without nails or screws
Rubber ramp lists 1,500 lb capacity
Grooves channel water away from the top
Weather resistant wording for entries
cons: Hard to move once it is pressed down
Little size detail in the listing
Adhesive may not suit every floor finish

products.name: Pepe Mobility 0.5 Inch Wheelchair Threshold Ramp
products.description:
Pepe Mobility supplies a half-inch ramp at 39.4 inches long that you trim with a utility knife. The top is textured for everyday traction, and the product is aimed at easing transitions between floor types inside the home. A trim-to-fit approach suits narrow bathroom and closet openings.

The listing offers no capacity figure in the details reviewed, so it is a lighter-duty pick. Indoor positioning also means wet or exterior entries should look elsewhere. A rise of half an inch fits many interior sills but not every one.

It is the only ramp here you cut to length, while Nuvium and Henka arrive at a set width near 35 inches. Silver Spring offers a rated capacity at a half inch if you want data over flexibility. Mark your line with a straight edge and cut in several light passes for a clean edge. For a doorway that is narrower than standard, this is the easiest to size.
products.bestFor: Narrow or unusual interior openings that need a custom length.

Half-inch rise matches typical sills
Textured top for everyday traction
Eases transitions between floor types
cons: No capacity figure in the details
Indoor focus rules out wet entries

products.name: Silver Spring Solid Rubber Threshold Ramp, 1/2 Inch Rise
products.description:
Silver Spring crafts this ramp from high-density molded rubber and states it supports up to 1,500 lb. It adds only a half inch of rise and is described as bridging doorways, thresholds, and small rises for wheelchairs, walkers, and scooters. The top is textured and includes drainage channels.

The weak spot is information. The listing in the details reviewed does not give width or depth, so check those with the seller. A loose rubber wedge also needs care so it does not shift underfoot.

It is the best-documented half-inch ramp for a device user, ahead of Pepe in stated capacity. Where Henka is glued and Nuvium is 0.6 inch, this one is a plain half-inch wedge that sits on the floor. Position it so the long edge meets the sill squarely. It is the sensible pick for a house with standard-height thresholds and a wheelchair or walker in daily use.
products.bestFor: Standard half-inch sills with a wheelchair or walker.

products.name: LIEKUMM 3/8 Inch Rubber Threshold Ramp for Doorways
products.description:
LIEKUMM supplies a 3/8 inch wedge that is 2 inches deep and 35.5 inches wide. Grooves give grip in dry or damp rooms, and the maker says the rubber is odorless, non-toxic, and weather resistant. The thin profile suits sills that sit almost flush.

Capacity is confusing, since the title claims 3300 lbs and a bullet lists 2,500 lbs. Treat the lower number as the working limit. It will not suit a typical half-inch sill, where a lip would remain.

A 2 inch depth over a 3/8 inch rise gives a slope near 1:5, similar to the Nuvium ramps. It is more appropriate than Silver Spring for a lower threshold, such as a tile edge. Use it only where the measured lip is close to three eighths of an inch. Press it flat and watch for slipping when first used.
products.bestFor: Low sills and tile edges near three eighths of an inch.

products.name: Nuvium 1 Inch Rise Rubber Threshold Ramp for Doorways
products.description:
Nuvium's taller model rises 1 inch over a 5.3 inch run and spans 35.5 inches. The maker states a 2,000 lb capacity, and deep grooves add traction on wet or dry surfaces. Dense natural rubber makes it suitable for indoor or outdoor use.

The slope, about 1:5, is steep for a manual wheelchair. The listing notes a mild rubber odor and a slight curve that may need time to relax. A one-inch sill is relatively rare indoors, so confirm you have one.

Most homes with a one-inch lip are older houses, garage entries, or sliding doors with a raised track. For those, this ramp avoids stacking two shorter wedges. For a half-inch lip, Silver Spring would be a better fit. Check the surface for any curl before use and set the ramp so the grooves run across the direction of travel.
products.bestFor: Raised tracks and taller one-inch sills.

cons: 5.3 in run makes a steep slope

buyingCriteria.criterion: Identify the type of sill first
buyingCriteria.explanation: Interior thresholds come in several forms. A bathroom sill is often a marble or wood strip near 0.5 inch, a sliding-door track can be about one inch, and a tile edge can be as low as 3/8 inch. Match them to Silver Spring at 1/2 inch, Nuvium at 1 inch, and LIEKUMM at 3/8 inch. Measure at the center of the door and at both ends, since sills are not always level.

Slope is run divided by rise. Nuvium 0.6 inch comes to about 1:5 and LIEKUMM is near 1:5 as well, while Silver Spring and Henka do not state the run in the details reviewed. Public ramps use 1:12, and retail advice often calls 1:6 the practical minimum for short rises. A steeper wedge is harder to push, so wheelchair users should lean toward the longest run available.

Add the person and the device and stay well under the stated rating. Nuvium states 2,000 lb, Henka and Silver Spring state 1,500 lb, and LIEKUMM lists conflicting values of 3300 and 2,500 lbs. Pepe gives no figure in the details reviewed. A rating is a maker's claim, so treat it as a margin, not an invitation.

Henka sticks down, Pepe is trimmed to length, and Nuvium, Silver Spring, and LIEKUMM sit on the floor. Adhesive prevents creep on tile but marks the floor if removed. Loose wedges move but can shift. Trimming gives a custom fit but cannot be undone. Decide which trade suits your flooring and your tolerance for changes.

Smooth tile and sealed hardwood let a loose wedge slide, while carpet traps edges. Bathrooms add water, so grooves or drainage channels such as Silver Spring and Henka offer help. Pepe is aimed at indoor transitions. Dry the floor and underside before placing a ramp, and wipe it after wet days.

Most interior doors need about 35 to 36 inches of ramp. Nuvium and LIEKUMM are 35.5 inches, and Pepe starts at 39.4 inches and can be cut. Check the clear opening between the door stops rather than the nominal door size. A ramp wider than the frame needs trimming, and one narrower leaves a gap.

howWeEvaluated.title: Interior fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each ramp to the interior sills it suits. LIEKUMM covers about 3/8 inch, Pepe and Silver Spring cover 1/2 inch, Nuvium and Henka cover 0.6 inch, and Nuvium 1 inch covers raised tracks. A ramp that fits only one narrow case still ranks well for that case.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slope information
howWeEvaluated.description: We calculated slopes where depth was given. Nuvium and LIEKUMM both land near 1:5. Listings without a stated run, like Henka and Silver Spring, lost points for transparency in this area.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on product specs and buyer feedback, we compared stated loads and flagged contradictions. Nuvium leads on clear data, LIEKUMM loses credit for conflicting numbers, and Pepe gives no figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation method
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at adhesive, trim-to-fit, and loose designs. Henka offers the firmest hold, Pepe the most adjustability, and the rest rely on weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value within the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every pick is at or under the cap, so we asked which listing tells you the most for your doorway. Nuvium wins on clarity, Silver Spring on a standard sill with rated load, and the others on a narrower use.

faq.q: How do I pick the right ramp height?
faq.a: Measure from the lower floor to the top of the sill with a ruler, and do so at several points along the door. Choose the ramp whose rise equals that number or is just above it. LIEKUMM suits about 3/8 inch, Silver Spring and Pepe 1/2 inch, Nuvium and Henka 0.6 inch, and Nuvium's tall model 1 inch.

faq.q: Should I glue or leave the ramp loose?
faq.a: Glue works well on smooth tile where a wedge might creep, as with Henka. Loose wedges are easy to move and clean but need regular checks. Test adhesive on a hidden spot first if the floor finish is delicate. Neither approach replaces careful placement.

faq.q: Can a ramp be cut to fit a narrow door?
faq.a: Pepe Mobility is designed to be trimmed with a utility knife from its 39.4 inch length. Most other ramps here are sized near 35.5 inches. Cutting a molded wedge that is not made for it is not advised. Check with the seller before altering any ramp.

faq.q: Is a ramp enough for a wheelchair user?
faq.a: A threshold ramp only handles a small lip. For stairs or steps you need a different ramp type with a gentler slope. The rule of thumb is a longer run for a taller rise. Ask an occupational therapist to confirm the slope suits the chair.

faq.q: Why does my new rubber ramp smell?
faq.a: Molded rubber can give off a mild odor at first, and the Nuvium listing mentions it. LIEKUMM calls its rubber odorless. Air the ramp out in a ventilated area for a day or two before laying it down.

faq.q: How can I tell if a ramp is sliding?
faq.a: Look for gaps at the sill edge, marks on the floor, or a ramp that has moved from its original line. Try pushing it gently with your foot before relying on it. If it moves, add a fixing method or switch to an adhesive model.

faq.q: Do these ramps help prevent falls?
faq.a: They make a small lip easier to cross, but no ramp can promise to prevent falls. Fit, slope, and floor conditions all matter. Keep the area dry and well lit, and cross slowly.
